bar_vectors.name: gapped-window
bar_vectors.why: Every session gaps away from the previous close, so the overnight-gap adjustment is the whole measurement: adjusted the window reads 128.9 bps, unadjusted it floors at zero. An implementation that omits the adjustment cannot pass this vector, and omitting it understates spread, which is the optimistic direction.

bar_vectors.name: contained-closes
bar_vectors.why: Every close sits inside the next session's range, so the adjustment must be a no-op: adjusted and unadjusted agree exactly. Pins that the shift does not fire where there is no gap.

bar_vectors.name: bar-window-short-refusal
bar_vectors.why: One excluded pair takes the same tape from 11 usable pairs to 10, one below MIN_USABLE_PAIRS. The estimators must refuse rather than report a thinner number that reads the same as a well-supported one.

estimator_contract.excluded_pairs: a per-PAIR boolean mask over the window's consecutive-session pairs, length len(bars) - 1, where true drops that one pair from every estimator alike. An implementation that excludes by DATE instead (Stock-Vault drops any pair either of whose dates is a confirmed split ex-date) is NOT equivalent: excluding a date drops BOTH pairs touching it. To drive these vectors it must realise a masked pair as a calendar hole between that pair's two sessions, which drops exactly the one pair. Getting this wrong changes usable_pairs and therefore which side of MIN_USABLE_PAIRS the window falls on.
estimator_contract.overnight_gap_adjust: always on. The adjustment is part of the model; the `unadjusted_cs_spread_bps` field exists to pin that it changes the answer where a gap exists and does not where none does, not to license an unadjusted estimate.
estimator_contract.refusal_layer: MIN_USABLE_PAIRS is a property of the COMPOSED estimate, not necessarily of the bare spread estimator. Stock-Grader enforces it inside corwin_schultz_spread_bps; Stock-Vault enforces it one level up, in estimate(). A vector whose `expected` is null must therefore be driven through whichever function owns the floor in that repository, and must produce a refusal there -- not a number.

units.amihud_lambda_bps_per_musd: bps of price per $1M traded. An implementation whose Amihud estimator returns the raw |r| / $volume ratio (fraction of price per dollar) must multiply by 1e10 -- 1e4 for bps and 1e6 for the $M -- before comparing against this field.
units.cs_spread_bps: FULL spread in bps of price, the window MEAN of the raw two-day Corwin-Schultz estimates, floored at zero on the mean and never per pair.
units.sigma: sample sd of daily log close-to-close returns over the window's usable pairs.
units.unadjusted_cs_spread_bps: same units as cs_spread_bps, with the overnight-gap adjustment switched off. Declared so an implementation can prove the adjustment fires; it is NOT an option the model offers a caller.
units.usable_pairs: count of consecutive two-day pairs surviving the exclusion mask.

estimator_contract.why: bar_vectors landed on the Stock-Grader side alone, and a literal port into Stock-Vault does not work: the two implementations agree on the model and disagree on units and on which function refuses. Both facts were unwritten, so the porting side had to guess. They are declared here, and a conforming implementation converts to them rather than the file bending to either repository's internals.

note: Cross-repository pin for the per-row trading-cost model. Stock-Grader (src/stock_grader/costs.py) and Stock-Vault (src/stock_vault/costs.py) implement this model independently because neither repository may import the other; this file is what keeps the two implementations from drifting apart in silence. `vectors` pins the COMPOSITION (liquidity inputs in, one cost estimate out); `bar_vectors` pins the ESTIMATORS themselves (raw daily bars in, spread/sigma/lambda out), which the composition vectors cannot reach because they take the spread as a scalar input; `estimator_contract` declares the units and the enforcement layer a conforming implementation must convert to before it can drive `bar_vectors` at all. HOW THE PIN IS ENFORCED, stated exactly and not more strongly than it holds: each repository carries this file and asserts the canonical sha256 below in its own test suite, which catches an edit to one copy that does not update that copy's literal, but NOT an edit landed in one repository and never landed in the other -- that is a convention between the two suites, not a test either of them can run alone. The check that closes it is one-directional and lives in Stock-Vault's CI, which fetches this file from the PUBLIC Stock-Grader main and refuses to build on any difference; the reverse direction is not checkable, because Stock-Grader's CI cannot read a private repository. An earlier revision of this note claimed the two copies were byte-identical as a matter of fact while they were not, which is the asserted-instead-of-computed failure the pin exists to prevent. Every input below is a synthetic round number chosen for arithmetic convenience: nothing here is measured from any archive, so the file is safe in a public repository. Tolerance: relative 1e-9. A change to this file is a change to the cost model and must land in both repositories in the same breath.

vectors.name: degenerate-flat-5bps
vectors.why: CS=0, tick floor exactly 10 bps, sigma=0, lambda=0, cap disabled: the historical flat charge, exactly. A change that breaks this vector changes every sim-v1 number ever recorded.

vectors.name: tick-floor-binds
vectors.why: A cheap name whose Corwin-Schultz estimate is narrower than one tick: the tick floor wins.

vectors.name: cs-estimate-binds
vectors.why: A higher-priced name whose Corwin-Schultz estimate is wider than the tick: the estimate wins.

vectors.name: athl-dominates-amihud
vectors.why: Model impact above the measured floor: impact is the ATHL term.

vectors.name: amihud-floor-binds
vectors.why: Measured floor above the model: the conservatism rule takes the larger of the two.

vectors.name: capacity-cap-truncates
vectors.why: A target of 5 percent of ADV is truncated to the 1 percent cap; participation is the cap and the truncation is reported, never applied silently.

vectors.name: short-window-refusal
vectors.why: Ten usable pairs is below MIN_USABLE_PAIRS: no estimate at all, rather than a thinly supported one that reads like a well supported one.
